stories.title: Northern Idaho’s rivers and gathering places
stories.subtitle: Idaho — northern river corridors
stories.description: Fishing and gathering on the Clearwater and neighboring rivers connect early archaeological evidence to Nimiipuu councils and two histories of mission building.

scenes.title: Encounter on Weippe Prairie
scenes.body: Lewis and Clark’s expedition met Nimiipuu at a place they used for gathering roots.
scenes.note: Documented day of encounter at an existing gathering place.

scenes.title: Spalding mission moves to the lower Clearwater
scenes.body: Henry and Eliza Spalding moved their mission and home from farther up the Lapwai Valley. Excavators later identified remains of the principal building and its additions.
scenes.note: Documented relocation year, with summer known.

scenes.title: Coeur d’Alene people help build Sacred Heart Mission
scenes.body: Coeur d’Alene tribal members and Catholic missionaries built the Sacred Heart mission church between 1850 and 1853.
scenes.note: Institutional construction interval. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Volunteers establish the Fort Lapwai post
scenes.body: Military volunteers established a post in the Lapwai Valley. In 1877 the fort served as a United States Army operations centre early in the conflict with the Nimiipuu.
scenes.note: Year of establishment, sourced season only.

scenes.title: Non-treaty bands gather at Tepahlewam
scenes.body: Several Nimiipuu bands gathered at Tepahlewam as US authorities pressed them to leave their homelands for a much smaller reservation.
scenes.note: Documented by date, not the first day of gathering.

stories.title: Rapa Nui from Anakena to Haŋa Roa
stories.subtitle: Rapa Nui
stories.description: Follow coastal platforms, quarry gardens and ceremonial sites into the period of colonial agreements and restrictions on Rapanui people.

scenes.title: Dated courtyard context at Ahu Nau Nau
scenes.body: Charcoal from a feature in front of the primary platform wall constrains the age of the first courtyard phase. The excavation identified multiple subsequent phases.
scenes.note: Calibrated two-sigma interval for a sample associated with the primary courtyard phase, separate from island arrival and construction dates of other features. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Cultivation in the Rano Raraku quarry
scenes.body: Among deposits on the inner quarry slopes are traces of cultivated plants, including sweet potato and taro. The archaeological team relates the quarry soil’s fertility in part to weathered stone debris.
scenes.note: Modelled age range for Zone I’s deposits, which date part of a longer cultivation history. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Early Birdman ceremonial activity at ‘Orongo
scenes.body: Samples support early seventeenth-century ceremonial activity by the village’s stone houses.
scenes.note: Broad early-seventeenth-century archaeological bracket. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Rapanui leaders and Chilean representatives record an agreement
scenes.body: Atamu Tekena and other Rapanui leaders negotiated with Policarpo Toro. The preserved proclamation documents the parties’ agreement in versions that carry materially different language.
scenes.note: Documented date of the proclamation.

stories.title: Crossing the mountains in western Montana
stories.subtitle: Montana — western mountains
stories.description: Painted shelters, trading posts and treaty grounds put several kinds of evidence on the routes across the northern Rocky Mountains.

scenes.title: Dated rock painting in the Big Belt Mountains
scenes.body: AMS analysis of pigment samples from three places, including Gates of the Mountains, produced overlapping ages. The paintings provide dated examples of activity in the west-central Montana mountain foothills.
scenes.note: Combined calibrated envelope published for three statistically indistinguishable estimates. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Hudson’s Bay Company establishes Fort Connah
scenes.body: The Hudson’s Bay Company opened a trading post in the Flathead Valley in the same year that the Oregon Treaty set an international boundary farther north.
scenes.note: Documented establishment year.

scenes.title: Fort Owen trading post is established
scenes.body: John Owen bought the former St. Mary’s Mission property and established a trading post in the Bitterroot Valley.
scenes.note: Documented establishment year.

scenes.title: Hellgate Treaty council near Missoula
scenes.body: Salish, Pend d’Oreille and Kootenai leaders met territorial officials. The treaty established the Flathead Reservation and left the future of Bitterroot Salish land contingent on a federal survey.
scenes.note: Documented treaty year, council held in July.

scenes.title: United States Army attacks a Nimiipuu camp
scenes.body: United States infantry and volunteers attacked a Nimiipuu camp in the Big Hole valley during the flight of the non-treaty bands. Nimiipuu families and Army troops suffered deaths in two days of fighting.
scenes.note: Start day of two-day fighting.

stories.title: Windward Islands and Barbados
stories.subtitle: Southern Lesser Antilles
stories.description: Ceramic-age settlements and changes in fishing connect Grenada, Carriacou and Saint Lucia. Records from Barbados and Saint Lucia trace resistance and emancipation in the plantation era.

scenes.title: Dated shell at Pearls
scenes.body: An analyzed shell from the Pearls archaeological site dates to the first millennium CE.
scenes.note: Calibrated bounds printed for a shell whose exact archaeological context is poorly documented. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Habitation deposits at Grand Bay
scenes.body: Midden deposits and other occupation features contain evidence assigned to several ceramic phases.
scenes.note: Rounded archaeological horizon across dated contexts. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Fishing and habitation at Sabazan
scenes.body: Fish bones show that people at Sabazan harvested a variety of marine species over the course of its use.
scenes.note: Approximate archaeological horizon; the record represents stratified evidence of fishing. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Late Ceramic Age village and burials at Lavoutte
scenes.body: Excavators identified remains of a village and burial areas on Saint Lucia’s northern coast.
scenes.note: Approximate span assigned to the site’s main ceramic horizon. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Rebellion at Bayley’s Plantation
scenes.body: Bussa and other enslaved Barbadians organized an uprising in 1816. The government identifies Bayley’s Plantation and Golden Grove as places affected.
scenes.note: Documented year. The plantation-scale record does not assign the full island-wide rebellion to a single point.

scenes.title: Soufrière’s plantation district at emancipation
scenes.body: Saint Lucia’s Pitons Management Area identifies Soufrière as a major slave plantation district when slavery ended.
scenes.note: Emancipation-era observation for the district.

stories.title: Caddo communities and inland Louisiana
stories.subtitle: Louisiana — northern / inland
stories.description: Red River evidence follows Caddo mound and village landscapes into the trading frontier between the French and Spanish outposts.

scenes.title: Early Caddo mortuary evidence at Mounds Plantation
scenes.body: The Red River mound center preserves early Caddo archaeological material associated with funerary contexts.
scenes.note: Approximate Caddo-period assignment for the archaeological material. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Late Caddo material at Belcher
scenes.body: Pottery, food remains and structures at Belcher document a later phase in the Red River valley.
scenes.note: Broad period for the archaeological phase named for the site. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: French forces are sent to build a Natchitoches fort
scenes.body: The French dispatched Charles Claude Dutisné and soldiers to build and garrison an outpost on the Red River at Natchitoches.
scenes.note: Year the construction and garrison party was sent.

scenes.title: Mission and presidio construction at Los Adaes
scenes.body: Spanish authorities built a mission and presidio near Natchitoches, where exchanges with neighboring peoples linked communities across the frontier.
scenes.note: Historical construction bracket. The viewing year falls within that range.

stories.title: Marshes and homelands of northwestern Nevada
stories.subtitle: Nevada — northwestern basins
stories.description: The western Great Basin’s wetlands supported skilled work. Later sources follow Northern Paiute resistance and educational initiatives alongside military and federal institutions.

scenes.title: Tule duck decoy from Lovelock Cave
scenes.body: The Smithsonian holds a Lovelock Cave decoy. Its shaping and material illustrate how Great Basin people used a wetland plant to make hunting equipment.
scenes.note: Museum age bracket for this object. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Pyramid Lake War
scenes.body: Northern Paiute and settlers fought around Pyramid Lake in 1860 amid encroachment and violence.
scenes.note: Documented year of conflict.

scenes.title: United States Army builds Fort Churchill
scenes.body: The Army constructed Fort Churchill to protect settlers and emigrant routes and to guard communication lines.
scenes.note: Documented construction year.

scenes.title: Sarah Winnemucca’s school near Lovelock
scenes.body: Sarah Winnemucca organized a school for Paiute children. Her ally Elizabeth Palmer Peabody documented the school in 1886.
scenes.note: Year covered in the school report and correspondence.

scenes.title: Stewart Indian School opens
scenes.body: The federal boarding school near Carson City opened for Native children in December 1890.
scenes.note: Documented opening date.

stories.title: Leeward islands of the northern Lesser Antilles
stories.subtitle: Northern Lesser Antilles
stories.description: Early ceramic-age sites and coastal settlements predate the forts and naval works built with enslaved labor.

scenes.title: Early Ceramic activity at Trants
scenes.body: Excavation and radiocarbon evidence place Trants among the earlier Saladoid-associated sites of the eastern Caribbean.
scenes.note: Approximate archaeological timeline date; does not establish an exact occupation onset.

scenes.title: Anse à la Gourde’s structures and deposits
scenes.body: Excavation along the coast at Anse à la Gourde found habitation structures and material from different periods of settlement.
scenes.note: Approximate range of dated and archaeologically assigned contexts. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: First documented military use at Brimstone Hill
scenes.body: British forces installed a cannon at Brimstone Hill in 1690. The larger fortress took shape in later phases through the labor of enslaved Africans.
scenes.note: First documented military use of the hill, when British forces mounted a cannon. The larger surviving fortress developed in later phases.

scenes.title: Naval works begin at English Harbour
scenes.body: British works began at English Harbour in 1725 as the navy developed a repair and support base. Enslaved workers supplied essential construction and maritime skills.
scenes.note: Documented year of early naval works, distinct from the standing complex’s later construction.

stories.title: Communities of Venezuela’s rivers, llanos and islands
stories.subtitle: Venezuela
stories.description: Compare work on the Orinoco, drained fields in the Barinas llanos, and maritime activity on the cays off Venezuela’s coast.

scenes.title: Archaeological evidence of changing maize use at Parmana
scenes.body: The Parmana team used isotopic and archaeological evidence to infer that maize became an important food at the site over a broad prehistoric period.
scenes.note: Broad author estimate for subsistence change. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Late Gaván settlement complex
scenes.body: Regional excavation and survey in Barinas identified habitation sites and land-use features associated with the Late Gaván phase.
scenes.note: Late Gaván phase bracket, associated with the settlement complex rather than every structure. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Drainage and agriculture at La Tigra
scenes.body: Archaeologists documented an engineered field system in the Barinas llanos and assigned it to Late Gaván activity.
scenes.note: Archaeological phase bracket. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Mainland animals and marine work at Dos Mosquises
scenes.body: Faunal remains and isotope evidence indicate that Indigenous visitors intentionally moved some animals from the mainland to Dos Mosquises during a period of seasonal resource use.
scenes.note: Approximate Late Ceramic Age bracket assigned to the excavated sites. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Nueva Cádiz receives city status on Cubagua
scenes.body: The settlement received formal city status in 1528 and became a trading and political center for pearl fishing. The people who performed the coerced labor lived and worked at separate fishery settlements.
scenes.note: Documented urban charter milestone, separate from earlier extraction and related work settlements.

stories.title: Fiji, Tonga and Samoa after initial settlement
stories.subtitle: Fiji / Tonga / Samoa
stories.description: Dune deposits in Fiji, earthworks in Tonga and a monumental mound on Savai‘i show how island communities reshaped very different landscapes.

scenes.title: Early flat-topped mound near Fua‘amotu
scenes.body: Radiocarbon results date early monumental construction near Fua‘amotu. The mound has nearby road traces and open space.
scenes.note: Bayesian highest-density interval for estimated mound construction. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Later occupation layers at the Sigatoka dunes
scenes.body: The dunes on Viti Levu preserve a later Navatu-phase archaeological occupation layer above earlier Lapita deposits.
scenes.note: Approximate calibrated phase, converted using 1950 as the reference year. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Early construction of Pulemelei mound
scenes.body: Archaeological study at Letolo dates the first large platform phase of Pulemelei mound to the first centuries of the second millennium.
scenes.note: Approximate initial phase, distinct from later additions. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Lagoon-edge reclamation at Lapaha
scenes.body: Radiocarbon results place reclamation along the lagoon as the Lapaha chiefly precinct developed.
scenes.note: Dated reclamation evidence, separate from tomb construction and settlement founding. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Fijian chiefs sign the Deed of Cession at Levuka
scenes.body: Fijian chiefs including Cakobau and British representatives signed the Deed of Cession at Levuka. The original document records the formal transfer of sovereignty claimed by its signatories.
scenes.note: Documented day and town on the deed.

stories.title: Baja California and the Sonoran desert
stories.subtitle: Northern Mexico / Baja
stories.description: Early coastal burials, earthen villages and hillside terraces show histories of land use that stretch well before the peninsula’s mission period.

scenes.title: Burial evidence at Bajamar–Jatay
scenes.body: INAH archaeologists report a group of burials placed beneath large grinding stones. They provide a calendar age bracket for one individual.
scenes.note: Published age range for one individual, with confidence level unreported in the bulletin. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Earthen architecture at La Ciénega
scenes.body: INAH excavations identified a village with earthen buildings in the Cocóspera valley. Archaeologists tentatively associate its development with earlier activity of the Trincheras tradition.
scenes.note: Preliminary archaeological date bracket, as reported by the project. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Terraced community at Cerro de Trincheras
scenes.body: On the volcanic hillside, residents built terraces that supported domestic, agricultural and craft activities.
scenes.note: Approximate principal settlement phase according to INAH’s archaeological interpretation. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Stone mission church at the relocated San Francisco Javier site
scenes.body: After its move to a place near a water source, work on the mission church began in 1744. The historic catalogue records completion in 1757.
scenes.note: Documented construction interval for standing church, distinct from the 1699 mission institution. The viewing year falls within that range.

stories.title: Society, Cook and Marquesas island histories
stories.subtitle: Societies / Cooks / Marquesas
stories.description: Waterlogged coastal deposits, Marquesan valleys, Society Islands marae and teachers crossing to Aitutaki connect distinct archipelagos over several centuries.

scenes.title: Waterlogged early coastal deposits at Fa‘ahia
scenes.body: Waterlogged deposits preserve perishable material from early Society Island activity, including wood and fiber objects.
scenes.note: New short-lived samples date the lowest cultural layer; later artifacts and older inbuilt-age samples are separate evidence. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Early dated activity in Hatiheu Valley
scenes.body: Excavation and AMS dating place early human use at Pahumanoo-te-tai in the late thirteenth to late fourteenth century.
scenes.note: Rounded historical range for the evidence of early local use. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Ceremonial coastal and valley landscape at Taputapuātea
scenes.body: The historical complex includes ceremonial marae near the coast and in the valleys, with the prominence of Taputapuātea linked to the Tamatoa chiefs.
scenes.note: Broad heritage chronology for examples in the complex, separate from any single building’s foundation. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Polynesian teachers arrive on Aitutaki
scenes.body: The Cook Islands Christian Church identifies Papeiha and Vahapata as teachers who arrived from the Society Islands with John Williams.
scenes.note: Documented date in the church’s historical account.

stories.title: Aotearoa’s coastal villages, pā and Māori political centers
stories.subtitle: Aotearoa New Zealand
stories.description: Early Māori coastal life, journeys of the treaty sheets, a fortified pā and the emergence of the Kīngitanga occupy different parts of Aotearoa.

scenes.title: Early community on the Waihemo coast
scenes.body: Studies of preserved material from an early Māori village near the Shag River mouth show daily subsistence and health evidence, including traces of intestinal parasites.
scenes.note: Radiocarbon dates from this part of the site fall within 1300–1500. The excavators infer that the occupation itself lasted about 20–50 years. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Te Tiriti signing occasion at Akaroa
scenes.body: A Treaty of Waitangi signing occasion at Akaroa is recorded for the Herald sheet.
scenes.note: Documented date of local signing occasion.

scenes.title: British and allied forces occupy Ruapekapeka pā
scenes.body: After a siege, British and allied Māori forces occupied the fortified pā that Kawiti and his people built. It was the final major action of the Northern War.
scenes.note: Published day of occupation, separate from the siege’s beginning.

scenes.title: Pōtatau Te Wherowhero is installed as Māori King
scenes.body: Pōtatau Te Wherowhero became the first Māori King at Ngāruawāhia in 1858, after discussions among supporters of the Kīngitanga.
scenes.note: Documented year with month available.

stories.title: Indigenous town landscapes of the Virginia Tidewater
stories.subtitle: Southeast / Tidewater
stories.description: Palisaded villages, raised and cut earthworks, treaty negotiations and a pottery school connect Indigenous histories across Tidewater waterways.

scenes.title: Palisaded Patawomeck village at Potomac Creek
scenes.body: Excavations and radiocarbon evidence document a palisaded village at Potomac Creek. Its setting is near, but distinct from, the village contacted in 1608.
scenes.note: Published inferred period of use at 44ST2. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Fifteenth-century landscape ditches at Werowocomoco
scenes.body: Paired ditches show how Indigenous residents reshaped this place on the York River before the documented colonial encounters.
scenes.note: Excavation-based date estimate for the pair of ditches. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Paspahegh household and settlement evidence
scenes.body: Settlement remains include post traces of longhouses along with ceramics and other locally recovered artifacts. The site provides evidence of a village within the Powhatan political landscape.
scenes.note: Broad ceramic and documentary bracket for the settlement’s later phase. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Cockacoeske signs the Treaty of Middle Plantation
scenes.body: Cockacoeske appeared as the Pamunkey leader and joined other parties in signing an agreement with colonial officials that addressed Indigenous land and hunting rights alongside obligations to the Crown.
scenes.note: Documented date on original treaty signature page.

scenes.title: Pamunkey Pottery School established on tribal land
scenes.body: Pamunkey potters and Virginia education officials organized a school for pottery production on the Pamunkey Reservation. The school helped develop a market for local wares.
scenes.note: Documented year of the school’s organization.

stories.title: Volcanic valleys and lakeshore communities in El Salvador and Nicaragua
stories.subtitle: Honduras / El Salvador / Nicaragua
stories.description: Volcanic deposits preserve different chapters of the Zapotitán Valley, while sites around Lake Nicaragua show changing households and ceramic traditions.

scenes.title: People use volcanic tephra to build at San Andrés
scenes.body: Excavation and modelling date the Campana structure’s tephra-and-earth construction phase several years after a major Ilopango eruption.
scenes.note: Modelled bracket for this construction phase; exact eruption year is a separate result. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Volcanic ash preserves the farming village at Joya de Cerén
scenes.body: An eruption covered the farming village with ash and preserved evidence of buildings and household life.
scenes.note: Approximate archaeological date for the volcanic deposit, not a village foundation year.

scenes.title: Late Bagaces deposits at El Rayo
scenes.body: Early samples and material culture document occupation at a lakeshore site later used during the Sapoá period.
scenes.note: Published two-sigma calibrated date bracket for sample Beta-265454. Dates of nearby deposits differ. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Dated houses and other domestic contexts at Santa Isabel
scenes.body: Excavations and radiocarbon dating support repeated use of the San Jorge lakeshore settlement during the Sapoá period.
scenes.note: Rounded observation envelope covering early and later dated contexts. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Dated archaeology at Tepetate
scenes.body: Excavation examined one of the surviving mounds and two small urn burial groups at the archaeological locality on the north side of Granada.
scenes.note: Two-sigma calibrated date range for sample Beta-257985, one of two dates in the published table. The viewing year falls within that range.

stories.title: Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego from the Atlantic to the Beagle Channel
stories.subtitle: Patagonia / Tierra del Fuego
stories.description: Calibrated evidence from coastal middens and Beagle Channel sites gives depth to a regional chronology that also records later colonial coercion.

scenes.title: Middle Holocene archaeological deposits at Túnel I
scenes.body: A separately dated component of Túnel I documents Indigenous activity along the Beagle Channel. The table reports animal remains from that archaeological component.
scenes.note: Published calibrated interval 4987–4566 cal BP, converted to the atlas’s year scale. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Dated midden deposit at Sitio Moreno
scenes.body: Dispersed charcoal from a shell midden at an open-air residential site dates a local episode on the north coast of Santa Cruz.
scenes.note: Published calibrated interval 2920–2729 cal BP for LP-206. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Dated guanaco bone at the Cabo Blanco midden
scenes.body: The lower layer at Cabo Blanco 1, an open-air shell midden, contained a dated guanaco bone. Its context documents terrestrial as well as coastal resources.
scenes.note: The table gives 1698–1475 calibrated years BP for a lower-level sample, converted against 1950. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Late archaeological evidence at Shamakush X
scenes.body: A calibrated date from Shamakush X provides evidence of late use in the Beagle Channel region many centuries after the middle-Holocene contexts at Túnel I.
scenes.note: Published 574–305 cal BP sample range, converted against 1950. The viewing year falls within that range.

scenes.title: Chile grants a lease for the Dawson Island mission
scenes.body: Chilean authorities granted a lease for the Salesian mission on Dawson Island. Selk’nam people were later taken to the mission by force.
scenes.note: Documented day of the government lease decree, distinct from mission founding or closure.
